The session runs to a fixed clock: **Build** 25 minutes, **Use** 20, **Reconcile** 15, **peer check** 5.
The move from Build to Use is called at minute 30 whether or not Build finished — an unfinished
Build is a legitimate finding, reported as one.

::: {.part}
### Part 1 · Before you arrive

Accounts and data only. Nothing here needs software installed at home.

1. Create a Taiga account at [tree.taiga.io](https://tree.taiga.io) with your NDSU email, and a private project named `IMSE456-yourlastname`.
2. Create the cloud folder you will use all semester — Google Drive or OneDrive, named `IMSE456`. **Everything in this course is saved there, never to a local disk.**
3. Open the access form linked on Blackboard and answer both questions: which machine you will work on, and which AI tooling you can reach. Two minutes, no effect on your grade — it decides which version of every later lab sheet you get.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 2 · What you will have at the end

SA1 — your Taiga sandbox URL, the <code>.pod</code>, the classification table, the paragraph
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 3 · Build it yourself — 25 minutes

1. Create your own Taiga account at <code>tree.taiga.io</code> and a private sandbox project named <code>IMSE456-yourlastname</code>. The team project comes later, at FP0.
2. Install ProjectLibre and open the supplied <code>.pod</code>. If it fails on your machine it fails <em>today</em>, not in Week 4 — and GanttProject is the sanctioned fallback.
3. Open the course Colab notebook and run the setup cell.
4. Claim your AI access: register the free student year at <a href="https://gemini.google/students/">gemini.google/students</a> if you are eligible, and install <a href="https://antigravity.google/">Antigravity</a>, which is free to everyone. If neither is available to you, the free Gemini tier is sufficient for every studio in this course — tell the instructor so it is on record.
5. Ask Gemini to generate six candidate initiatives for a campus organization. Classify each as project, operation, or hybrid using the temporary-and-unique test — and record every one the model classified wrongly.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 4 · Now the professional tool — 20 minutes

1. Enter the three you classified as projects into your Taiga sandbox as epics.
2. Enter the same three into ProjectLibre as summary tasks with placeholder durations.
3. Write down what each tool <em>forced</em> you to state that the other did not.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 5 · Where do they disagree? — 15 minutes

Which tool made you commit to something you did not yet know? One paragraph, naming the specific field.

Write one paragraph. **This is the graded part** — it is the only thing here a machine cannot check.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 6 · Run the check

Run the `verify()` cell at the end of the notebook. It tests your own outputs against tolerances and
prints a completion code. If it fails, you have found your error while it is still cheap to fix —
that is the point of it. Paste the code into your submission.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 7 · Done looks like — the checklist your neighbour runs on you at minute 65

- [ ] Taiga account created and the sandbox project exists
- [ ] the .pod opens on your machine or you have reported the failure
- [ ] AI access claimed or reported
- [ ] six items classified with a written justification each
- [ ] the paragraph names a specific field
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 8 · Where it is saved

`IMSE456/studio-01/` in your cloud folder. Name files `SA1_yourlastname.*`.

**Nothing in this course is saved to a local disk.** Lab machines wipe on reboot and laptops get
left at home. Submit the PDF and the completion code to Blackboard by the due date above.
:::

::: {.browser-path}
**Working on lab machines?**

**No ProjectLibre?** Do the *Use* half in Smartsheet instead — indented WBS, Gantt, predecessors and critical path all work in a browser. Say so in your submission; it costs you nothing.

**No Antigravity?** Use the Gemini API from the course Colab notebook — the key is in the shared config cell. Same work, browser only.
:::

## Study loop for this week

Run this before you read the notes, and again after. It is not graded; it is the fastest way to find out what you have wrong.

```text
Be my tutor on what "project success" means and why it's contested. Ask me
one question at a time. Don't lecture. Start by making me define success,
then attack my definition. Push until I admit it's multidimensional, then
make me name the dimensions myself.
```

See [AI Studio](../ai.qmd) for the Editor and Roommate prompts and the full loop.


::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Label it, verify it, own it.** Append the AI acknowledgement block from the [syllabus](../syllabus.qmd#how-to-disclose): the tool, the prompt or transcript link, what you changed after reviewing its output, and what it got wrong. Every quantitative result arrives with the check that proves it — **the check is graded, not the output**. "The model said so" is not a defence in this course or in a project review.
:::
